social.title: Europe's Best Bar: Line, Petralona
social.description: A former art gallery in Kato Petralona, run zero-waste by the Clumsies team, named the single best bar in Europe in 2026 and pouring drinks nobody else is making.
social.bonus: Order whatever the bar is most proud of rather than whatever sounds familiar.

social.title: Natural Wine at Materia Prima
social.description: A Koukaki cava and wine bistro near the modern art museum built around low-intervention Greek producers, where the owner will pour you things by the glass to argue about.
social.bonus: Drink a grape variety you've never heard of and remember the name.

social.title: Panoramic Drinks at 360
social.description: A rooftop on Ifaistou in the middle of Monastiraki with a genuinely 360-degree turn from the Acropolis round to Lycabettus, open from ten in the morning until three.
social.bonus: Identify all three ancient hills visible from the roof.

social.title: Greek Craft Taps at Barley Cargo
social.description: A rustic room on Kolokotroni open from midday to three in the morning, with a tap list built almost entirely from Greek microbreweries and coolers full of the rest.
social.bonus: Drink only Greek breweries and find one worth taking a can of home.

social.title: Rebetiko Until Dawn at Kavouras
social.description: A first-floor room in an Exarchia neoclassical building where live rebetiko — the Greek urban blues, on UNESCO's heritage list — runs Friday and Saturday until it gets light.
social.bonus: Stay past two in the morning, when the crowd starts singing along.

social.title: The Roof at A for Athens
social.description: A rooftop directly over Monastiraki metro with the Acropolis filling one entire side of the view, busy from six until the small hours every night of the year.
social.bonus: Get there before sunset to claim a rail seat facing the rock.

social.title: Rum on Klitiou at Baba Au Rum
social.description: A small bar on a pedestrian lane with one of Europe's deepest rum collections, twelve consecutive years on the World's 50 Best list and a queue on the steps outside.
social.bonus: Let the bartender choose a rum flight and guess the countries.

social.title: Vermouth and Pizza at Odori
social.description: Greece's first vermuteria, on Agioi Theodoroi square, pairing house vermouth cocktails with pizza that has been ranked among the best in Europe.
social.bonus: Drink the vermouth neat over ice before you order a cocktail with it.

social.title: Two Hundred Greek Wines at Heteroclito
social.description: A corner wine bar near Syntagma stocking only Greek bottles, more than two hundred of them, with staff who will take you through Santorini Assyrtiko to Naoussa Xinomavro.
social.bonus: Try one white and one red from islands you've never been to.

social.title: Cocktails at The Clumsies
social.description: A neoclassical townhouse off Praxitelous that has been on the World's 50 Best Bars list every year since it opened, building Greek botanicals into everything it pours.
social.bonus: Ask to sit in the back Playroom rather than the main bar.

social.title: The Courtyard at Six d.o.g.s
social.description: A hidden garden courtyard off Avramiotou that runs as a café by day and a gig venue and club by night, open every day of the year with free entry to the garden.
social.bonus: Stay from daylight through to the first band without leaving.

social.title: Ouzo at Brettos
social.description: Athens' oldest distillery, operating in the same Plaka mansion since 1909, with a back wall of backlit bottles stacked to the ceiling and thirty-five house liqueurs.
social.bonus: Drink the house ouzo the proper way, with water and no ice.

chill.title: Digging Through Monastiraki Flea Market
chill.description: The Sunday sprawl around Avissynias Square, where genuine Greek antiques, old brass, military surplus and complete junk are laid out side by side on the pavement.
chill.bonus: Haggle for one thing you have no practical use for and win.

chill.title: Coffee in Plateia Varnava
chill.description: A square in Pangrati with no sights at all, ringed by café tables under plane trees, where Athenians spend three hours over one freddo espresso as a matter of routine.
chill.bonus: Order one freddo and genuinely make it last two hours.

chill.title: An Hour at Little Tree Books
chill.description: A small Koukaki bookshop-café round the corner from the Acropolis Museum, with handmade cake, a shelf of English titles and no pressure to leave.
chill.bonus: Buy a Greek author in translation and start it there.

chill.title: A Sunbed Day at Varkiza
chill.description: The full organised Greek beach experience at the end of the Riviera: sunbeds, umbrellas, beach bars bringing drinks to your lounger, and showers before you head back in.
chill.bonus: Stay through the changeover from afternoon sunbathers to evening drinkers.

chill.title: Filter Coffee at Taf
chill.description: A roastery on Emmanouil Benaki at the edge of Exarchia staffed by competition baristas, where Athens' specialty coffee scene effectively started.
chill.bonus: Ask for the current single origin as filter and drink it without sugar.

chill.title: The Hammam Ritual at Al Hammam
chill.description: A marble Ottoman-style bathhouse in Plaka a hundred metres from the ancient Baths of the Winds, doing the full steam, scrub and soap-foam sequence.
chill.bonus: Take the full scrub rather than just the steam room.

chill.title: A Film Under the Parthenon at Cine Thisio
chill.description: Athens' oldest open-air cinema, running since 1935: a jasmine-scented walled garden with tables for two, wine from the kiosk, and the floodlit Parthenon above the screen.
chill.bonus: Take the late showing so the Acropolis is lit for the whole film.

chill.title: The Island Lanes of Anafiotika
chill.description: A Cycladic village built into the north slope of the Acropolis by stonemasons from Anafi in the 1840s: whitewashed steps, bougainvillea and lanes too narrow for a car.
chill.bonus: Get properly lost and come out somewhere you didn't expect.

chill.title: The Roof Lawn at the Niarchos Centre
chill.description: Renzo Piano's cultural centre with a park built over the top of it, sloping up to a hilltop lawn where you can see the Acropolis one way and the sea the other.
chill.bonus: Walk up the whole slope to the roof rather than taking the lift.

chill.title: Lost in the National Garden
chill.description: Queen Amalia's 1840 garden behind parliament: fifteen hectares of dense shade, ancient column fragments used as benches, duck ponds and a temperature ten degrees below the street.
chill.bonus: Find the Roman mosaic floor hidden among the trees.

culture.title: The Museum of Cycladic Art
culture.description: Rooms of marble figurines from the Cycladic islands, 5,000 years old and so reduced and abstract that Brancusi and Modigliani spent their careers chasing them.
culture.bonus: Pick the figurine you'd most believe was made last year.

culture.title: Sunset at the Temple of Poseidon
culture.description: Doric columns on a cliff at Cape Sounion, seventy kilometres down the coast, where Byron carved his name and the sun goes down into the Aegean behind the temple.
culture.bonus: Find Byron's signature on the column before the light goes.

culture.title: A Night at the Odeon of Herodes Atticus
culture.description: A Roman theatre from AD 161 built into the Acropolis slope, still used every summer for the Athens Epidaurus Festival, with the lit Parthenon directly above the stage.
culture.bonus: Sit high enough up that the Acropolis is in frame above the performers.

culture.title: The Antikythera Mechanism
culture.description: The National Archaeological Museum holds the greatest collection of Greek antiquities anywhere, including the Mask of Agamemnon and a 2,000-year-old geared astronomical computer.
culture.bonus: Find the Antikythera Mechanism and read the whole reconstruction panel.

culture.title: First Entry to the Acropolis
culture.description: The Parthenon, the Erechtheion and the Propylaea on their rock, worth booking the very first slot of the day for: an hour on the summit before the heat and the crowds.
culture.bonus: Be through the gate in the first ten minutes of opening.

culture.title: The Benaki Museum of Greek Culture
culture.description: One family's collection filling a Kolonaki mansion, running from neolithic pottery through Byzantine icons to whole carved rooms lifted out of Ottoman-era Macedonian houses.
culture.bonus: Find the two complete wooden reception rooms and stand inside one.

culture.title: The Ancient Agora and the Hephaisteion
culture.description: The square where Socrates argued and Athenian democracy actually functioned, with the best-preserved Greek temple in the world standing complete on the rise above it.
culture.bonus: Walk the Panathenaic Way through the site rather than round the edge.

culture.title: The Parthenon Gallery at the Acropolis Museum
culture.description: A glass top floor aligned exactly with the temple itself, displaying the surviving frieze at its original spacing with plaster casts standing in for the pieces in London.
culture.bonus: Walk the full frieze in narrative order and find where the casts begin.

8ball.title: Wildcard: Ride the Line to the End
8ball.description: Get on the metro at Monastiraki, take whichever line arrives first all the way to its final station, and eat lunch within five minutes' walk of wherever you come out.
8ball.bonus: Ask someone at the terminus where they'd eat and go there instead.

8ball.title: Wildcard: Five Rooftops, One Night
8ball.description: One drink on five different Athens rooftops in a single evening, starting before sunset and ending after midnight, and the Acropolis has to be visible from every single one.
8ball.bonus: Photograph the rock from each roof and put them in order of how good the view was.

foodie.title: A Michelin Star on the Roof at Hytra
foodie.description: Modern Greek cooking on the top floors of the Onassis Cultural Centre, with a summer terrace giving a 360-degree turn from the Acropolis round to the sea.
foodie.bonus: Book the outdoor terrace and time it for sunset.

foodie.title: Varoulko Seaside
foodie.description: Lefteris Lazarou's restaurant on Mikrolimano harbour, the first in Greece ever to win a Michelin star, still built entirely around fish and still holding it.
foodie.bonus: Take the tasting menu and ask which dish has been on it longest.

foodie.title: Charcoal Chops at Telis
foodie.description: A fluorescent-lit Psyri room that has grilled one dish since 1977: thin pork chops from Epirus over charcoal, piled on hand-cut chips, no starters, no fuss.
foodie.bonus: Order the full portion and finish the chips as well.

foodie.title: Lunch at Diporto, Unmarked
foodie.description: A basement taverna by the central market with no sign, no menu and no printed bill, open since 1887: you get whatever was cooked that morning and wine from the barrel.
foodie.bonus: Eat everything put in front of you without asking what it is.

foodie.title: Gelato at Le Greche
foodie.description: Italian technique and Greek ingredients on Mitropoleos: mastiha, fig and mascarpone, Bronte pistachio, churned in small batches and open until midnight.
foodie.bonus: Order a flavour that only exists because of a Greek ingredient.

foodie.title: The Varvakios Central Market
foodie.description: A cast-iron nineteenth-century hall on Athinas Street: hanging carcasses on one side, ice-packed fish on the other, and spice shops in the streets around it.
foodie.bonus: Walk the full length of the fish hall before you eat anything.

foodie.title: Souvlaki at Kostas
foodie.description: A single counter on Agia Irini square, open since 1950, making one thing: pork souvlaki with a house spicy tomato sauce, until it sells out and shuts for the day.
foodie.bonus: Get there before one o'clock and eat it on the church steps.

foodie.title: Dinner Under the Acropolis at Strofi
foodie.description: A 1975 taverna on the Makrygianni slope whose roof terrace puts the floodlit Parthenon directly over your table, with lamb and smoked aubergine to match.
foodie.bonus: Book a roof table and sit facing the rock, not the room.

foodie.title: Yoghurt and Galaktoboureko at Stani
foodie.description: A 1931 dairy shop near Omonia serving its own thick set yoghurt with honey and walnuts, plus a galaktoboureko of crisp filo over warm semolina custard.
foodie.bonus: Have the yoghurt as well as the pastry, not instead of it.

foodie.title: Tyropita at Ariston
foodie.description: A tiny pie shop on Voulis Street run by the same family since 1910, whose half-moon cheese pie in butter pastry is the standard the whole city is judged against.
foodie.bonus: Buy two: the classic tyropita and whatever seasonal pie they're doing that week.

foodie.title: Fish at Mikrolimano
foodie.description: Papaioannou on the Piraeus fishing harbour, with yacht masts a metre from the table, where the whole fish is chosen from ice and charged by the kilo.
foodie.bonus: Pick your own fish at the counter instead of ordering from the menu.

foodie.title: Loukoumades at Krinos
foodie.description: The same Aiolou Street shop since 1923, frying honey-soaked dough balls to order and serving them scalding hot with cinnamon in a room that hasn't been redecorated since.
foodie.bonus: Eat the first one immediately, before it stops being too hot to handle.

adventure.title: Blue Hour on the Areopagus
adventure.description: A bare marble outcrop below the Acropolis entrance, polished slippery by 2,500 years of feet, where St Paul preached and where half of Athens now watches the light go.
adventure.bonus: Get up the rock and back down again without using the metal staircase.

adventure.title: Cycle the Athens Riviera
adventure.description: A flat coastal run from Faliro out past the marinas to Vouliagmeni, sea on one side the whole way, with a swim stop wherever you feel like stopping.
adventure.bonus: Swim at three different beaches before you turn round.

adventure.title: Hydra: No Cars, Just the Coast Path
adventure.description: An island where wheeled vehicles are banned outright, reached from Piraeus in ninety minutes, with a stone coast path west from the harbour to swimming platforms at Vlychos.
adventure.bonus: Walk the whole path and swim at the far end rather than taking a water taxi.

adventure.title: Dawn on the Grand Promenade
adventure.description: The pedestrianised marble boulevard under the south slope of the Acropolis, walked at first light when it belongs entirely to runners, dog walkers and street cats.
adventure.bonus: Get from Thissio to the Acropolis Museum before the first tour group appears.

adventure.title: Float in Lake Vouliagmeni
adventure.description: A collapsed cave lake on the Athens Riviera fed by underground thermal springs, holding 22 degrees all year beneath a sheer rock face, with tiny fish that clean your feet.
adventure.bonus: Swim right up to the cliff wall at the far end.

adventure.title: A Lap of the Panathenaic Stadium
adventure.description: The all-marble stadium that hosted the first modern Olympics in 1896, rebuilt on a fourth-century BC track, and you are allowed onto the running surface itself.
adventure.bonus: Run a full lap of the track, hairpin bends and all.

adventure.title: Snorkel the Kavouri Rocks
adventure.description: A rocky headland thirty minutes from the centre where the water drops away fast and clear over seagrass and boulders, and there's almost always somebody spearfishing further out.
adventure.bonus: Stay in long enough to find an octopus.

adventure.title: Bungee the Corinth Canal
adventure.description: A jump platform bolted to a bridge over the Corinth Canal, eighty metres above a strip of green water between two sheer walls of rock cut by hand in the 1890s.
adventure.bonus: Go head first rather than feet first.

adventure.title: Sunrise on Lycabettus Hill
adventure.description: A steep pine-scented switchback path up the highest hill in Athens, ending at a whitewashed chapel with the Acropolis below you and the Saronic Gulf beyond it.
adventure.bonus: Walk up rather than taking the funicular, and do it before the heat arrives.

adventure.title: Up Hymettus from Kaisariani Monastery
adventure.description: A trail from an eleventh-century monastery in a replanted forest up the mountain that gives Athens its famous violet evening light, with the whole basin below you.
adventure.bonus: Start at the monastery rather than driving up, and go inside before you set off.

adventure.title: Ferry to Aegina for the Day
adventure.description: Forty minutes on a fast boat from Piraeus to an island with a fifth-century temple on a pine ridge, pistachio groves, and a fishing village lunch at Perdika.
adventure.bonus: Rent a scooter at the port and get to the Temple of Aphaia before you eat.

adventure.title: Parnitha to the Flabouri Refuge
adventure.description: Athens' only national park and its highest mountain, an hour north: fir forest, red deer, and a mountain refuge serving lentil soup at 1,150 metres.
adventure.bonus: Eat at the refuge rather than carrying your own lunch.

adventure.title: Climb the Hymettus Crags
adventure.description: Bolted limestone sport routes on the flanks of Mount Hymettus, twenty minutes from the centre, where the Athens climbing scene goes after work in winter.
adventure.bonus: Time a route so you're on the wall as the city lights come on below.

adventure.title: Cliff Swim at Limanakia
adventure.description: A run of unorganised rocky coves south of Vouliagmeni with no sunbeds and no entrance fee, where Athenians scramble down the rocks and jump straight into deep clear water.
adventure.bonus: Find a cove with nobody else in it and jump from the highest ledge you're comfortable with.

adventure.title: Sunset on Filopappou Hill
adventure.description: Marble paths laid by Dimitris Pikionis wind through pines and ruins to a Roman monument with the best free head-on view of the Parthenon in the city.
adventure.bonus: Find the stretch of Pikionis paving and notice it's made of recycled ancient stone.

adventure.title: Windsurf at Varkiza
adventure.description: A big organised beach resort at the far end of the Riviera with a reliable afternoon thermal, board hire, instructors, and wakeboarding and paddleboards if the wind dies.
adventure.bonus: Stay out until you can hold a run the full length of the bay.
